# One source-preserving posterior feedback on its guarded positive domain

This is the SAME rational feedback T(p),K(p) as in the independently received local tree-completable construction, but stopped on an explicitly defined larger feasible domain rather than a tiny probability cube. There is no claim that an entire arbitrary larger cube satisfies the inequalities: the inequalities themselves define where this controller runs.

The four free coordinates are z=(p3,p5,p6,p7). Solve p4=p5(3p6+p7)/(2p7), set a base vector with p0=p1=0 and p2 chosen to normalize, and let d=(1,1,-2,0,0,0,0,0). Since q(Yd)=0 exactly, global q-balance is LINEAR in the adjustment a along d. The receipt gives its exact rational solution. Thus p(z) is an explicit smooth rational chart, not a numerical projection or an assumed implicit branch.

Take the source-connected domain where every p_i>p_i(original)/32, the absolute fixed pivot determinant and the Hessian-Gram determinant exceed1/64 of their exact source values, K>I/1024, and RR^T>I/64 with R=YT. All inequalities are exact rational or Loewner inequalities. The source lies strictly inside, as checked by exact principal minors. Its closure in the probability simplex is compact and all rational denominators stay away from zero; K is uniformly positive. The Frobenius projection formula also bounds ||K||_F<=||I||_F=2. Thus the coefficients and their local derivatives are bounded on the guarded closure.

Run dz=K(p(z))^(1/2)dW and stop at its first domain exit. Because the free rows of T equal I, the induced diffusion in the full probability vector has covariance TKT^T. Its Itô drift vanishes: differentiate the constraint equations, and use their exact half-Hessian trace cancellations; the invertible pivot forces the pivot-coordinate drift to zero. Therefore all p_i and the mean m=Yp are bounded martingales. This is the same no-drift posterior construction as the local receiver, not a projected numerical process.

Mean covariance is RKR^T>=I/65536. Optional-stopping localization gives E tau <=(65536/3) E|Y|^2, because E|m_(t wedge tau)|^2<=E|Y|^2. Hence the first exit is finite almost surely with finite expected occupation. At exit every posterior probability is still at least its positive floor; all tree constraints still hold by continuity. Attach the exact updated original3-level null tree, then the original downstream policy. Opt
